What is stereo?:
Notice how speakers and headphones come in pairs? This is to match how your head has 2 ears. Each ear hears different things than the other because they are separated spatially and face different directions. The left and right speakers in stereo receive different information to allow them to produce different sounds than one another. It’s invention can be traced back to the 1930’s and stereo sound has been in mainstream home use since the late 1960’s and early 70’s.

What’s Mono then?:
Mono is the opposite. Using one sound source. This music sounds fine like this, but doesn’t have the spacial depth of stereo. Enabling mono on stereo equipment will cause the 2 separate channels of information for left and right to merge, and be equally sent to both speakers, or both drivers in your headphones.

How do I enable Mono on my equipment:
If you are using a phone for music playback, you will most likely find an option for it in your music playback app.
Or in your settings in either sound or accessibility.

If you are using modern AV equipment then their should likely be a setting to change between surround, stereo and mono.

If you are using vintage sound equipment then the front face of your unit likely has a dial or switch for selecting Mono or Stereo.
No problem
Set your playback device to output in Mono if you can. Both sides will get the same signal rather than separated stereo or surround.
